name: Recognise addition and subtraction as inverses
description: Student can recognise that addition and subtraction undo each other.
commonError: Student treats the two operations as unrelated.
checkpointTask: Give an addition fact. Ask the student for the related subtraction.

name: Write a fact family
description: Student can write the family of addition and subtraction facts for three numbers.
commonError: Student writes only one or two facts, or includes facts that do not belong.
checkpointTask: Give three related numbers. Ask the student to write the whole fact family.

name: Find an unknown in a number sentence
description: Student can find an unknown value in an addition or subtraction number sentence.
commonError: Student adds the two visible numbers regardless of where the unknown is.
checkpointTask: Pose number sentences with the unknown in different positions. Ask the student to solve each.

name: Use the inverse to find an unknown
description: Student can use the inverse operation to find an unknown.
commonError: Student subtracts when they should add to undo the operation.
checkpointTask: Pose sentences where the inverse is needed. Ask the student to find the unknown.

name: Recall addition and subtraction facts to 20
description: Student can recall addition and related subtraction facts to 20.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked 9 + 7, the student answers 16 without counting.
commonError: Student counts on from materials every time rather than recalling.
checkpointTask: Quickfire facts to 20. Listen for recall rather than counting.

name: Extend a fact to larger numbers
description: Student can extend a known fact to a related larger calculation.
commonError: Student treats the larger calculation as unrelated to the known fact.
checkpointTask: Give a basic fact. Ask the student to use it for a related tens or hundreds calculation.

name: Use a mental partitioning strategy
description: Student can use partitioning to add or subtract larger numbers mentally.
exampleOfSuccess: For 53 + 28, the student adds 50+20 then 3+8 to get 81.
commonError: Student tries to hold all digits at once and loses track.
checkpointTask: Pose two-digit additions. Ask the student to solve mentally and explain the strategy.

name: Derive a subtraction from an addition
description: Student can derive a subtraction fact from a known addition fact.
commonError: Student recalculates from scratch rather than using the known addition.
checkpointTask: Give an addition fact for larger numbers. Ask for the related subtraction.

name: Recall the 10 multiplication facts
description: Student can recall multiplication facts for 10.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked 7 x 10, the student answers 70 straight away.
commonError: Student adds a zero without understanding, or miscounts groups.
checkpointTask: Quickfire 10 times facts. Listen for recall.

name: Recall the 5 multiplication facts
description: Student can recall multiplication facts for 5.
commonError: Student skip counts slowly each time rather than recalling.
checkpointTask: Quickfire 5 times facts. Listen for recall.

name: Recall the 3 and 4 multiplication facts
description: Student can recall multiplication facts for 3 and 4.
commonError: Student confuses the 3 and 4 facts, or relies on repeated addition.
checkpointTask: Quickfire 3 and 4 times facts. Listen for recall.

name: Recognise the pattern in the 5 facts
description: Student can recognise that multiples of 5 end in 5 or 0.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says any answer in the 5 times table ends in 5 or zero.
commonError: Student does not notice the pattern, or thinks it applies to other tables.
checkpointTask: Show the 5 times table. Ask the student what pattern they notice in the answers.

name: Derive a division fact from a multiplication fact
description: Student can use a known multiplication fact to state a related division fact.
exampleOfSuccess: Knowing 4 x 5 = 20, the student says 20 divided by 5 = 4.
commonError: Student cannot connect the multiplication and division facts.
checkpointTask: Give a known multiplication fact. Ask the student for a related division fact.
